definition: In computer vision, maximally stable extremal regions (MSER) technique is used as a method of blob detection in images.
details: This technique was proposed by Matas et al. to find correspondences between image elements taken from two images with different viewpoints. This method of extracting a comprehensive number of corresponding image elements contributes to the wide-baseline matching, and it has led to better stereo matching and object recognition algorithms.

explainer.lead: Maximally stable extremal regions (MSER) is a blob detection technique in computer vision. It was proposed by Matas et al. to find correspondences between image elements from two images taken from different viewpoints.

tiers.eli5: It finds blotches in a picture that stay the same shape even when the picture is taken from a different angle.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use MSER to extract many corresponding image elements for wide-baseline matching; the pitfall is that stability thresholds need tuning, since regions that are not truly stable will not match across views.
tiers.paperLevel: Detects extremal regions that remain maximally stable across a range of intensity thresholds; the many correspondences it yields support wide-baseline matching.

explainer.example: Matching two photos of the same building shot from far apart, MSER extracts stable blobs in each so corresponding points can be paired.
